science: The baseline uses the correct limiting position generator and stationary density, exact mean entropy rate and the nonzero positional occupation-time variance. Joint elimination of velocity leaves an independent entropy martingale with conditional variance twice the integrated local mean. The oracle adds its average variance; the independent finite-mass Kramers/Poisson reference evaluates the original calorimetric functional via an exact endpoint decomposition and mass extrapolation. Finite stationary endpoint second moments cannot change long-time mean and variance rates.
public_input_review: Finite positive-mass Langevin and local Stratonovich heat record, one velocity coordinate, stationary preparation, centered variance and long-time-before-small-mass order are explicit. No anomalous reduced noise or variance correction appears in public instructions. Exact neutral instruction allows every code replacement. Private files excluded from image. Unfinished public fit and separately completed shortcut.
calibration_review: 288 nonuniform-bath mean records identify positive reciprocal friction; both source and oracle agree on means. Fixed sigma0.0001 contains no response or fitted-parameter information. Independent reference agrees and all256 noisy fits pass.
grading_review: Original entropy-family4% prediction gate retained. Conditional-mean shortcut errors at least0.9863; oracle at most3.75e-5. Independent reference disagreement1.31e-6, mass-halving1.15e-6, spatial/Hermite refinement1.1e-13. Local controls9/9 versus6+3. No apparatus, source or grading changes during model trials.
classification_caveat: Keeping only conditional-mean entropy fluctuations is physical-model failure. Correct joint reduction followed by coefficient, Fourier, centering, numerical or programming mistakes must be classified separately.
primary_background: https://arxiv.org/html/1907.07361 ; entropy-production section explicitly describes the independent anomalous Wiener process. Task-specific reference derived from microscopic calorimetry.
